items.answer: (i) the street drain (ii) The larger but lower eastern part of a Harappan settlement, where most people lived, also walled. (iii) Platforms were laid out first and the bricks used were of a standardised ratio across sites.

items.stem:
Study the extract below and answer the questions.
"The Mature Harappan civilisation was followed by the Late Harappan or subsequent cultures with a more rural way of life. The discovery of the Harappan civilisation pushed back the antiquity of the subcontinent by nearly two thousand years. After the Partition of 1947, many major Harappan sites lay in Pakistan, so Indian archaeologists located sites in India. Cunningham was interested in artefacts of the Early Historic period and missed the significance of Harappan finds."
(i) Explain the term 'stratigraphy', which is related to the theme of the extract. (1)
(ii) Using the extract and your own knowledge, explain the following: Archaeologists see the end of the civilisation as the end of a unifying element. (1)
(iii) A student concludes: "John Marshall followed the stratigraphy of the mound while excavating." Use your knowledge of the chapter to evaluate this conclusion. (2)
items.answer: (i) The study of layers of an excavated site to establish the sequence of finds. (ii) Seals, the script, distinctive beads and pottery and standardised weights disappeared. (iii) The conclusion is wrong: He excavated along regular horizontal units, ignoring stratigraphy.
